title: Heading Hierarchy

illustrates.quote: The order of braille heading hierarchy is as follows: centered, cell-5, cell-7. (See Sample 4-2: Heading Hierarchy on page 4-17.) Additional provisions governing the use and placement of headings are given in other sections of these guidelines.

blocks.features: Centered, large bold blue-black serif title heading.
Bold black run-in-style heading, indented beneath the ELA code heading.

blocks.text: Some types of bacteria have been used to help clean up oil spills in oceans or in lakes. Gather information about how the bacteria were used, and prepare a report. Share your findings with the other students in your class.
blocks.features: Plain body text (instructions) for the Writing activity.
Bold blue, left-aligned, standards-code sub-heading, same visual level as "Writing ELA—W 2.3".
Bold black run-in-style heading, indented beneath the SDAP code heading, same visual level as "Write a Report".

blocks.text: Healthy soil has large numbers of decomposers living in it. One gram of soil (much less than an ounce) can contain 100,000 algae, 1,000,000 fungi, and 100,000,000 bacteria. Make a bar graph comparing the numbers of these types of decomposers in the soil.
blocks.features: Plain body text (instructions) for the Math activity.

print.notes: Illustrates the centered/cell-5/cell-7 heading hierarchy of rule 4.2.2: a centered major heading ('Make Connections'), then two cell-5 subject-code headings, each immediately followed (no blank line) by its own cell-7 task heading, per rule 4.5.7.
print.printFeatures: Boxed "Make Connections" callout; two parallel activity blocks, each with a bold blue standards-code sub-heading and a bold black task-name heading, followed by plain instructional body text.
